newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel forex-linked credit higher in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Israel forex-linked credit higher in 1997.

text.p: Israel's central bank said on Tuesday that the share of foreign currency linked credit in total bank credit rose from 22 percent in 1994 to 32 percent in the first half of the year.
The share of unlinked credit fell from 42 percent to 32 percent and the share of consumer price index (CPI) linked credit remained at 36 percent.

The monetary department of the Bank of Israel said that in the first half of 1997 the nominal average cost of the total credit the public took from banks in Israel and from foreign sources was an annualised 17.6 percent against 16.4 percent in 1996.

The cost of credit in the first half of 1997 was made more expensive because of the significant rise in the cost of foreign exchange linked credit - which rose from 11.7 percent in 1996 to 18.1 percent in the first half of 1997 - and because of the rise of the share of foreign currency linked credit in total bank credit.
